morphology.formula: ∅ + blackwood → blackwood；英语内部构成为 black + wood
morphology.pattern_note: 依资料包作为独立输入词处理，没有马来语词缀；is_root 不表示它是马来语固有词。英语内部为复合词，不能把 black 或 wood 当作马来语词缀。未获证实的马来语派生词不予列造。

senses.zh_definition: 英语树木通名，可指若干不同树种；澳大利亚语境中常指黑木相思树 Acacia melanoxylon，African blackwood 则指东非黑黄檀 Dalbergia melanoxylon。
senses.en_definition: An English common name for several trees, including Acacia melanoxylon; African blackwood denotes Dalbergia melanoxylon.
senses.ms_definition: Nama umum bahasa Inggeris bagi beberapa jenis pokok; Australian blackwood merujuk kepada Acacia melanoxylon, manakala African blackwood merujuk kepada Dalbergia melanoxylon.
senses.nuances: 资料包没有 DBP 释义，本次未核实其为 DBP 规范马来语词条；status 按指定模板填写，不代表 DBP 认证。此处马来语释义是解释性编写。树种须结合地域修饰语或学名确认，不能一概译为乌木。依据：[澳大利亚国家植物园](https://www.anbg.gov.au/acacia/species/species.html)、[英国皇家植物园 Kew](https://mpns.science.kew.org/mpns-portal/plantDetail?dbs=wcs&plantId=2755721)。

senses.zh_definition: 以 blackwood 为英语通名的树木所产的木材；实际材种随产地及树种而异。
senses.en_definition: The timber of a tree called blackwood, with the species determined by context.
senses.ms_definition: Kayu daripada pokok yang dikenali sebagai blackwood; jenis kayu yang dimaksudkan bergantung pada spesies dan asalnya.
senses.nuances: 用于木材、家具或乐器讨论时是英语名称的嵌入使用。Australian blackwood 与 African blackwood 不是同一树种，也不能仅凭名称断定木材必为纯黑色。若原文 Blackwood 是姓氏、地名或品牌，则不适用此木材释义。依据：[维多利亚州农业部门](https://agriculture.vic.gov.au/crops-and-horticulture/plantations-and-farm-forestry/farm-forestry-toolkit/species-guides/blackwood)、[Kew：Dalbergia melanoxylon](https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn%3Alsid%3Aipni.org%3Anames%3A490328-1/general-information)。

etymology.historical_story: English blackwood combines black and wood, but the name does not identify a single botanical species. Australian usage includes Acacia melanoxylon, while African blackwood names Dalbergia melanoxylon. Their different identities explain why the same familiar trade word can require a scientific name in a precise description. No historical borrowing into standard Malay is established here. Sources: [ANBG](https://www.anbg.gov.au/acacia/species/species.html) and [Kew](https://mpns.science.kew.org/mpns-portal/plantDetail?dbs=wcs&plantId=2755721).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: black 是黑，wood 是木：先记“木材名称”，再问“哪一种树”，别直接等同于乌木。

etymology.historical_story: Berkurung is transparently formed from Malay kurung with the prefix ber-. Its dictionary senses connect physical enclosure with the placement of writing inside brackets. The expression perintah berkurung extends the indoor sense into public administration, while the Brunei water sense preserves another concrete image of containment. These connections explain its semantic range without requiring a speculative ancient origin.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: kurung 联想“围住”；berkurung 就是“处在围住的范围内”：人待屋里，字待括号里。

etymology.historical_story: The cited dictionary records berambus as a forceful expression for going away, without establishing its deeper historical origin. Adding -lah places it within a familiar Malay pattern of emphatic commands. In dialogue, that familiar particle can make a dismissal sound sharply final; it does not erase the hostility carried by the verb.

etymology.historical_story: Two borrowing histories meet in this spelling. The military noun comes from Sanskrit bala, associated with strength and armed forces; the calamity noun comes from Arabic balāʾ, meaning affliction or trial. Their identical Malay spelling conceals different origins. Remembering two separate historical routes helps prevent the mistaken idea that an army somehow became a disaster semantically. See [bala etymologies](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/bala).

etymology.historical_story: The base manfaat is identified by DBP as an Arabic borrowing. Malay adds its own prefix ber- to express having benefit, producing bermanfaat. The same borrowed base also supports memanfaatkan, meaning to put something to good use. This family illustrates how an imported word becomes part of Malay vocabulary through ordinary Malay word formation. See [DBP: manfaat and derivatives](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=10456&keyword=bermanfaat).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: ber- 表示有，manfaat 表示益处：有益处 → bermanfaat。把 ilmu yang bermanfaat 连成一块记：有益的知识。

etymology.historical_story: The word belongs to the Malay lawan family, whose meanings include an opponent, a counterpart and competition. Malay affixation connects these ideas with opposing actions and contrasting relationships. Berlawanan therefore covers both people competing and things pointing different ways. This account concerns its transparent Malay formation, without assigning an unsupported ancient origin. See [DBP's entry](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=10456&keyword=berlawanan).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 抓住 lawan“对手”：对手站在另一边，所以 berlawanan 可表示意见对立、互相竞争，也可表示方向相反。

etymology.historical_story: Bible ultimately comes from Greek biblia, meaning books. That plural origin preserves an important cultural clue: the scriptures form a collection of writings rather than a single composition. In Malaysian usage, the English name appears alongside Malay religious terminology, including Alkitab, reflecting the country's multilingual Christian communities. [Etymological source](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bible)

etymology.historical_story: Brothers is the regular modern plural of brother, an inherited English kinship word recorded in Old English as brōthor. Related forms survive in other Germanic languages, including German Bruder and Dutch broeder. Its family meaning also supports figurative uses for solidarity and religious membership. Malay translations additionally distinguish older brothers from younger ones. [Oxford word origin](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/us/definition/english/brother_2)

morphology.formula: bersama + -an → bersamaan；进一步分析为 ber- + sama + -an
morphology.pattern_note: 按词包保留直接基底 bersama；更深层的词根是 sama。末尾 a 与后接 -an 的 a 分属两个音节，构成 ma.an，不合并为长元音；此处 ber- 无形态变化。

senses.zh_definition: 在日期或时间上相对应、相吻合；恰逢。
senses.en_definition: To coincide with or correspond to a particular date or time.
senses.ms_definition: Bertepatan atau berbetulan dengan sesuatu tarikh atau waktu.
senses.nuances: 常用于说明不同历法的对应日期，也可表示时间重合。这里不表示人们一起做事。释义依据 [DBP：bersamaan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=150348&keyword=bersamaan)。

senses.zh_definition: 在特征、性质或表现上近似；大致相同。

senses.ms_definition: Hampir sama atau hampir serupa.
senses.nuances: 这个义项表示相似或接近，不保证完全一致。需要表达毫无差异时，可用 sama sepenuhnya 或 serupa sepenuhnya。

senses.zh_definition: 在数量、数值、比例或换算关系上相当于；等于。
senses.en_definition: To be equivalent to a stated quantity, value, or amount under a given conversion or scale.
senses.ms_definition: Berbandingan atau berimbangan dengan sesuatu kuantiti, nilai atau ukuran.
senses.nuances: 常用 bersamaan dengan 引出换算结果。精确换算与近似估算须由数字、单位及 kira-kira 等限定语区分。

senses.zh_definition: 与某理论、原则或情况相符合、相适应。
senses.en_definition: To accord with or be consistent with a theory, principle, or circumstance.
senses.ms_definition: Berpadanan atau sesuai dengan sesuatu.
senses.nuances: 偏书面语，强调相符或适配；不能一律理解为数值相等。日常表达中也常用 selaras dengan 或 sesuai dengan。

senses.zh_definition: 在等级、地位、资格或层次上相当；同级。
senses.en_definition: To be equivalent or comparable in rank, standing, qualification, or level.
senses.ms_definition: Setara, sebanding atau setingkat dengan sesuatu.
senses.nuances: 比较不同制度的职级或学历时，是否获正式承认须看有关机构的规定；词语本身不构成资格认证。

etymology.historical_story: The family built around sama connects sameness with togetherness, comparison, and equivalence. Bersamaan makes that connection especially visible: DBP records uses involving coinciding dates, resemblance, proportional quantities, agreement, and comparable rank. A useful cultural setting is the explanation of corresponding calendar dates, where two different date expressions identify the same day. [DBP entry](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=150348&keyword=bersamaan)

senses.zh_definition: 【英语词】砖；用于砌墙或建造房屋的坚硬块状建筑材料，通常呈长方体。
senses.en_definition: A rectangular block of hard material used in building walls and houses.
senses.ms_definition: Perkataan bahasa Inggeris yang bermaksud batu bata, iaitu bongkah bahan keras, biasanya berbentuk segi empat tepat, yang digunakan untuk membina dinding dan bangunan.
senses.nuances: 此项解释英语原词；在标准马来语中通常使用 batu bata。输入没有提供可据以认定其为马来语普通词的DBP释义。status 沿用所要求的数据状态，不表示DBP收录。以下搭配为英语搭配，马来语对应分别为 dinding bata 和 bata merah。[英语释义](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/brick)。

senses.zh_definition: 【英语技术口语】使电子设备“变砖”；使设备因严重的软件或固件问题而无法正常启动或使用。
senses.en_definition: To make an electronic device unable to function, typically through a serious software or firmware problem.
senses.ms_definition: Dalam slanga teknologi bahasa Inggeris, menyebabkan peranti elektronik tidak dapat berfungsi, lazimnya akibat masalah perisian atau perisian tegar yang serius.
senses.nuances: 属于英语技术用法，可出现在马来语与英语混用的聊天中；并非所有死机或短暂故障都算 brick。标准马来语应按实际情况说明 peranti tidak dapat berfungsi 或 peranti gagal dihidupkan。以下搭配同样保留英语原形。[英语词条](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/brick)。

etymology.historical_story: English brick has medieval antecedents associated with Dutch and neighbouring Germanic languages. Its concrete building sense later supplied a technological metaphor: a disabled electronic device becomes about as useful as a brick. This history concerns an English word; encountering it inside a Malay conversation illustrates language mixing rather than, by itself, an established Malay borrowing. [Historical discussion](https://blog.oup.com/2009/11/brick/), [English meanings](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/brick).

etymology.historical_story: Because developed from the Middle English expression by cause that, which introduced a reason. The expression became a single conjunction rather than a productive combination of modern prefixes. Its historical structure belongs to English; it does not make because a Malay derivative or an established Malay headword. See [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/because).

etymology.historical_story: The botanical English noun bud continues Middle English budde and is recorded from the fourteenth century. Its image of small, developing growth also supports figurative uses. The conversational address bud has a separate relationship with buddy; it should not be explained as a plant metaphor. See [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bud).

senses.zh_definition: 需要；须有或须使用某人、某物。主要见于印度尼西亚语的特定语法结构，如 yang kita butuhkan，意为“我们所需要的”。马来西亚标准马来语通常用 perlukan 或 memerlukan，须依句法选择。
senses.en_definition: To need or require; an Indonesian verbal form occurring in constructions such as yang kita butuhkan, meaning ‘what we need’.
senses.ms_definition: Memerlukan; bentuk bahasa Indonesia yang digunakan dalam binaan seperti yang kita butuhkan, dengan padanan bahasa Melayu Malaysia yang kita perlukan.
senses.nuances: 输入只提供了 butuh I 的粗俗名词义，不能将其直接移植为派生动词 butuhkan 的释义。DBP 同时收录标为 Id（印度尼西亚语）的 butuh II，并以 memerlukan 解释 membutuhkan、membutuhi；但这不等于将 butuhkan 单列为马来西亚标准词条。[DBP：butuh](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=10456&keyword=butuh)。yang kita butuhkan 确见于印度尼西亚官方教育文章，因此也不能一概判为错误或不规范的印度尼西亚语。[印度尼西亚教育部门用例](https://gtk.kemendikdasmen.go.id/news/detail/indonesia-membutuhkan-guru-penggerak-di-berbagai-penjuru-negeri)。以下搭配属于印度尼西亚语，不作为马来西亚本地常用搭配教授。

collocations.zh: 我们需要什么；我们所需要的东西

dual_scenarios.context: 职场翻译报告：以标准马来西亚马来语讨论印度尼西亚语原文
dual_scenarios.ms: Dalam laporan ini, frasa bahasa Indonesia “yang kita butuhkan” diterjemahkan sebagai “yang kita perlukan”.
dual_scenarios.zh: 本报告将印度尼西亚语短语“yang kita butuhkan”译为马来西亚马来语的“yang kita perlukan”，意为“我们所需要的”。
dual_scenarios.en: In this report, the Indonesian phrase “yang kita butuhkan” is translated into Malaysian Malay as “yang kita perlukan”, meaning “what we need”.

dual_scenarios.context: WhatsApp / 马来西亚朋友讨论印度尼西亚语消息
dual_scenarios.ms_spoken: Dia tulis “yang kita butuhkan” kat WhatsApp tadi. Maksudnya “yang kita perlukan” je.

dual_scenarios.en: They wrote “yang kita butuhkan” on WhatsApp earlier. It just means “what we need”.

cultural_pragmatics.politeness_note: 对马来西亚客户、长辈或同事表达“需要”时，优先使用 perlu、memerlukan，或在适当结构中使用 perlukan。DBP 将同形词 butuh I 标为粗俗的男性生殖器称呼，因此脱离印度尼西亚语上下文时可能引起尴尬；不能据此认定印度尼西亚人使用“需要”义就是失礼。[DBP：语域与义项](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=10456&keyword=butuh)
cultural_pragmatics.usage_etiquette: 适合在印度尼西亚语阅读、原文引用、翻译说明及跨境交流中辨识。马来西亚公文或日常表达宜采用本地对应词。教学时应明确区分两个义项，避免将粗俗名词义误加到 butuhkan 上，也避免把印度尼西亚语正常表达当成黄色笑话。

etymology.historical_story: This word illustrates how closely related languages can give familiar forms different social associations. DBP distinguishes a vulgar Malay noun butuh from an Indonesian-labelled verb family meaning ‘need’. Butuhkan belongs with the latter in Indonesian constructions. These dictionary facts explain the cross-border misunderstanding; they do not establish when the meanings arose or whether one historically developed from the other. [DBP entry](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=10456&keyword=butuh)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把整块 yang kita butuhkan 记成“我们所需”，再配对马来西亚表达 yang kita perlukan。连句记，比只背 butuh 更能避免语境误会。

etymology.historical_story: Berkelip combines the Malay prefix ber- with kelip. Its meanings connect a tiny bodily movement with an intermittent visual effect: eyelids briefly close, while lights briefly disappear. The same family gives sekelip mata, an expression measuring time through a blink. This is a semantic connection, not evidence of a separately documented ancient origin. See [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=123312&keyword=kelip).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 ke-lip 想成眼皮轻轻一合一开：眼睛 berkelip，灯也能一明一灭地 berkelip。

senses.nuances: 英语名词复数。马来语通常用 lubang、liang 或 lubang sarang，并按动物及环境细化；不必机械使用重叠词表示复数。[Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/burrow)

senses.nuances: 比喻动作，不一定真的挖洞；通常与 into 连用。具体翻译依主语和动作选择钻进、偎入或埋入。[Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/burrow)

senses.zh_definition: 寄生虫在皮肤内或皮肤下形成的细小隧道，复数。
senses.en_definition: Small passages made in or beneath the skin by parasites.

etymology.historical_story: Burrow is recorded in English from the thirteenth century, with Middle English borow in its history. The noun names an animal's underground shelter, while the verb describes digging or moving as though digging. Burrows adds the ordinary English ending -s, marking either several shelters or an action performed by a singular subject. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/burrow)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 burrow 想成兔子钻入地下洞道的画面：名词是“洞”，动词是“钻、挖”。看到 burrows，先看句子是在说多个洞，还是一个主语正在挖洞。

etymology.historical_story: English biff belongs to the expressive vocabulary of sudden blows. Oxford dates it to the mid-nineteenth century and describes its origin as symbolic of a short, sharp movement. Its punchy sound helps explain its suitability for action writing. This English history does not establish that the packet contains an accepted Malay borrowing. [Oxford](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/biff_1).

etymology.historical_story: Baron has a long European history. Medieval French used it for an important lord before later systems gave it a more specific place among noble titles. Malay records both a British rank and a broader European nobleman sense. These overlapping meanings explain why a historical passage may require more context than a modern list of titles. See the [Académie française dictionary](https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A9B0462).

etymology.historical_story: Bocah belongs to the Javanese contribution to the region’s shared vocabulary. Its basic meaning is simply a child, although Malaysian readers may encounter it especially in regional speech or storytelling. The recorded expression bocah angon, a child herder, connects the word with rural life. Its origin is also documented in the Indonesian government’s [etymological dictionary](https://repositori.kemendikdasmen.go.id/23879/1/KAMUS%20ETIMOLOGI%20BAHASA%20INDONESIA.pdf).

etymology.historical_story: Personal names travel through Malay texts without becoming Malay vocabulary in the ordinary dictionary sense. Bennie is attested as a personal name, but the supplied lowercase token has no identifying context. Its bearer, source language, and naming history therefore remain unresolved. A responsible entry preserves that uncertainty instead of inventing a Malay origin or an official meaning.

etymology.historical_story: Bebe illustrates how identical spellings can conceal separate lexical histories. Kamus Dewan lists an Indonesian clothing term, a Dutch-derived administrative term, and a Kedah word for a nursing infant. These labels document different linguistic settings; they do not prove a shared origin. The available evidence does not establish a precise borrowing route for the clothing sense. See [DBP PRPM](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=54140&keyword=bebe).

etymology.historical_story: Braga preserves the memory of Bracara Augusta, its Roman predecessor. The city's municipal history project explains that Bracara is generally associated with the Bracari people or their territory, while Augusta honours Augustus. The name therefore carries both local and Roman history. In Malay, Braga functions as an unchanged foreign place name. Source: [Braga municipal history project](https://bragaromana.cm-braga.pt/).

etymology.historical_story: Bakinya illustrates how Malay builds reference into an ordinary noun: baki identifies what remains, while -nya points back to something already understood. The packet quotes a different dictionary sense of baki, meaning everlasting. Keeping those senses apart prevents a theological definition from being mistakenly attached to everyday talk about leftovers and balances. [DBP dictionary evidence](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=baki)

senses.nuances: 这是英语词或马英夹杂形式，不应作为规范马来语拼写教授。DBP 拼写指南明确列出 beer → bir；本条马来语释义采用规范对应词 bir 的词典解释，不能冒称存在 beer 的官方马来语释义。root beer 等固定英语名称须另行辨义，不能一律据名称判定含酒精。[DBP 拼写指南](https://eseminar.dbp.gov.my/dokumen/ejaan.pdf), [DBP：bir](https://prpmv1.dbp.gov.my/Search.aspx?k=minuman)

etymology.historical_story: English beer goes back to Old English bēor and has relatives in other Germanic languages. Its deeper origin remains debated, so a neat Latin origin should not be presented as certain. For Malay learners, the important later development is spelling adaptation: DBP explicitly gives beer → bir. The English spelling can still appear in mixed-language conversation and product labels. [Merriam-Webster](https://scrabble.m-w.com/dictionary/beer), [DBP](https://eseminar.dbp.gov.my/dokumen/ejaan.pdf)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: beer 的两个 e，进入马来语规范拼写时合成一个 i：beer → bir → 啤酒。这是拼写记忆提示，不是构词拆分。

etymology.historical_story: Babita is attested as a personal name in South Asian public records. Its appearance in a Malay word list does not establish a Malay lexical origin or a common noun meaning. Without the original sentence or the name bearer's linguistic background, a more specific origin story would be speculative. See the [Goa Government Gazette](https://goaprintingpress.gov.in/downloads/2526/2526-48-SIII-OG.pdf).

etymology.historical_story: Babai reflects the adaptation of English bye-bye into Malay conversational spelling. A Malaysian teacher-education publication records it among English expressions reshaped in SMS usage. Its familiar farewell function also appears in university language materials. These attestations illustrate everyday language contact; they do not establish a precise borrowing date or support deriving the word from baba. [Malaysian SMS study](https://ipkent.edu.my/document/pskent/pskent18/jpm/bahasa2015.pdf)

morphology.pattern_note: ber- 在 t 前保持原形，词根 tulis 的首音 t 保留；这里表示具有文字或已成文字的状态。

etymology.historical_story: Bertulis combines the Malay prefix ber- with tulis, the root associated with writing. The formation describes something bearing writing or existing in written form. Its cultural significance appears in the contrast between spoken agreement and a lasting written record. Today, the same expression bridges handwritten documents, printed letters and electronic correspondence without requiring a different root for each medium.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: tulis 是“写”；ber- 在这里提示“有这种状态”：bertulis 就是有字、写成了文字。secara bertulis＝以书面形式。

etymology.historical_story: Kamus Dewan places babe within Jakarta usage and connects it with baba in the sense father. That regional label matters: a dictionary can document a familiar family word without recommending it for Malaysian official correspondence. The supplied evidence establishes its meaning and regional association, but does not establish a deeper historical borrowing route.

morphology.formula: se- + belah → sebelah; ber- + sebelah + -an → bersebelahan
morphology.pattern_note: 以 sebelah 为直接构词基础，添加 ber-...-an；原有 h 保留并进入末音节 han。root_word 和 root_jawi 按数据包保留；实际基础为 sebelah（سبله），更底层词根为 belah（بله），因此修正数据包的 is_root=true。

etymology.historical_story: Bersebelahan can be understood through sebelah, meaning a side or the space beside something. The derived form presents that spatial relationship as a state: two people, rooms, or buildings occupy neighbouring positions. Its everyday meaning also supports technical uses such as adjacent angles. The connecting idea is position beside another entity, rather than simply being somewhere nearby. [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=72508&keyword=bersebelahan).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 先记 sebelah＝旁边，再想两把椅子并排：bersebelahan＝彼此就在旁边。

etymology.historical_story: Bisikan grows transparently from bisik, associated with speaking softly, and the noun-forming suffix -an. Its meanings connect an audible whisper with less tangible messages: private rumours, inward promptings, and inspiration. This semantic network explains why the same word can describe speech near someone's ear or a thought that seems to arise quietly within the heart.

etymology.historical_story: Malay dictionaries connect berkecai with kecai, a base associated with fragmentation. The prefix ber- forms the familiar predicate describing something in pieces. Dictionary senses extend from shattered glass to shredded cloth or paper, then to destroyed hopes. This connection provides a concrete route into the figurative meaning; it does not establish when that meaning first appeared. [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=54140&keyword=berkecai)

etymology.historical_story: Berbagi combines ber- with bagi in its giving or dividing sense. It illustrates how related Malay and Indonesian vocabularies can favour different everyday expressions. Indonesian commonly uses berbagi for sharing, while Malaysian Malay generally favours berkongsi. Recognising this relationship helps readers understand regional songs, videos and charitable slogans without assuming identical usage in every country.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: bagi 有‘给、分给’的意思：berbagi 就是‘一起分、一起分享’；在马来西亚日常说 berkongsi 更自然。

etymology.historical_story: Tumbuk connects pounding with blows delivered by the fist. With ber-, bertumbuk commonly describes people exchanging punches, while older dictionary uses include pounded rice and several kinds of contact or encounter. The pestle and the fist provide a useful cultural image linking these meanings; they do not, by themselves, prove the word's earliest origin or the order of its semantic development.

etymology.historical_story: Bangkitkan combines bangkit, associated with rising or awakening, with the Malay suffix -kan. Its meanings connect physical movement with mental and social activity: a sleeper wakes, enthusiasm rises, and an issue enters discussion. This connection is a useful semantic interpretation, not a dated account of how each meaning developed. Dictionaries also preserve the religious sense of raising the dead.

etymology.historical_story: Budapest's name joins Buda and Pest, formerly separate towns beside the Danube. The modern capital emerged in 1873 through the unification of Buda, Pest, and Óbuda. The name therefore offers a compact reminder of urban history: one familiar place name preserves the identities of older settlements brought together under a shared administration. [Source: Budapest City Archives](https://bparchiv.hu/150-eves-budapest/).

etymology.historical_story: Binasa is traced to Sanskrit vināśa, meaning destruction or ruin. The connection places it among Malay words reflecting historical contact with South Asian languages. In Malay, its force is both physical and moral: property can be destroyed, while a life can be ruined. Proverbs about speech preserve this warning of serious consequences in everyday cultural memory.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 binasa 的声音联想成“必拿去烧”，想象物品烧得毁坏殆尽；这是记忆联想，不是词源。

etymology.historical_story: English blade descends from Old English blæd, associated with leaves and flattened, leaflike parts. Its meanings connect grass leaves with the flat working surfaces of tools, including cutting implements. That shared shape helps explain why a knife, a fan and a plant can all have a blade, although their functions differ. [Source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/blade).

etymology.historical_story: DBP places bertembung under tembung II, distinguishing it from tembung I, a club or cudgel. Its recorded meanings connect encounters between people, joining rivers, colliding vehicles, and meeting eyes. These related images offer a useful cultural picture of paths coming together, although they do not establish which meaning developed first. See [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=tembung).

etymology.historical_story: The dictionary preserves two meanings of bersubahat: harbouring doubt and cooperating in a wrongful undertaking. Contemporary DBP advice foregrounds the second meaning. The contrast is useful when reading older material: context determines whether the passage concerns suspicion or complicity. This documented semantic range does not establish which meaning developed first. [DBP：词义记录](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=bersubahat)

etymology.historical_story: The Malay base tingkah names conduct, quirks or troublesome antics. Adding ber- turns that base into an activity: displaying such behaviour. The expression bertingkah laku broadens the meaning to conduct generally, allowing praise as well as criticism. DBP also records a discordance sense, so the surrounding words determine whether behaviour or sound is intended.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 tingkah 联想到“举动”，ber- 表示做出来：bertingkah 是做出怪举动；接上 laku，再看举止好坏。

etymology.historical_story: Bajrangi belongs to a Hindi naming tradition associated with Hanuman. The related name Bajrang is explained through Sanskrit vajra, a thunderbolt or diamond, and anga, a limb or body. The film Bajrangi Bhaijaan uses this devotional background for its protagonist, a Hanuman devotee helping a lost child. See [Miśra](https://threadreaderapp.com/scrolly/1424204611242663939) and [Salman Khan Films](https://www.salmankhanfilms.com/movies/bajrangi-bhaijaan).

etymology.historical_story: Bajak belongs to the vocabulary of cultivation, and Malay verse places membajak beside the figure of the farmer. A separate dictionary meaning identifies a sea robber, familiar in bajak laut. These two meanings offer contrasting cultural scenes, the cultivated field and the sea, but their shared spelling alone does not establish a common historical origin. [Malay Concordance Dictionary](https://www.malaycivilization.com.my/kamusmelayu/)

etymology.historical_story: Barbie entered the toy world in 1959, when Ruth Handler introduced an adult fashion doll through Mattel. Watching her daughter Barbara play with paper dolls helped inspire the idea. The name therefore belongs to a commercial character and brand, rather than to Malay word formation. Malay speakers can use that unchanged name inside otherwise Malay sentences. [Mattel history](https://creations.mattel.com/blogs/inside-look/barbie-65th-anniversary-inspiration-through-the-decades).

etymology.historical_story: This form illustrates how Malay builds a whole instruction around an adjective. Bersih names a clean state; -kan turns that state into an action, and -nya points back to an object already mentioned. The same vocabulary reaches beyond washing utensils: Malay also speaks of cleansing hearts, reforming institutions, and clearing reputations. See [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=243192&keyword=bersih).

etymology.historical_story: English base has more than one historical source. The noun meaning foundation came through French and Latin from Greek basis. etymology.historical_story: Berniaga carries a history of contact with South Asian trading vocabulary. Historical linguistic scholarship connects older beniaga forms with Indic words for merchants and records a related form in Pigafetta's 1521 vocabulary. Modern Malay transparently relates berniaga to niaga, but that present-day analysis should be distinguished from the older borrowing history. See [historical linguistic discussion](https://sealang.net/archives/nusa/pdf/nusa-v19-p1-38.pdf).

etymology.historical_story: Bhaijaan combines bhai, meaning brother, with Persian-derived jaan, meaning life or soul and also conveying affection. Urdu brings the elements together in a warm, respectful family address. It illustrates how a kinship term can carry both closeness and deference. Its appearance inside Malay conversation is best understood as contextual language mixing unless established borrowing is independently documented. [Jaan reference](https://rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-jaan-1).

etymology.historical_story: The important lexical distinction here is between an English word and its established Malay counterpart. DBP lists English bag with Malay equivalents including beg, karung and guni, depending on the container. This entry therefore treats bag as English material within Malay conversation, without inventing a separate historical Malay borrowing or an unsupported date of adoption. senses.zh_definition: 身体部位因受伤、疾病等而比正常状态肿大或隆起的。
senses.en_definition: Swollen or enlarged, especially of a body part affected by injury or illness.
senses.ms_definition: Lebih besar atau menonjol daripada keadaan biasa pada bahagian tubuh akibat penyakit, kecederaan dan sebagainya.
senses.nuances: 描述肿胀状态，不等于已经确定病因，也不必然表示化脓。表示逐渐肿起来时常用 membengkak。释义依据 [DBP《Kamus Dewan》及《Kamus Pelajar》](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=85408&keyword=bengkak)。

etymology.historical_story: Bengkak belongs to the everyday vocabulary of bodily experience. Malay also carries it into social commentary: the proverb lain bengkak, lain bernanah describes one person bearing the consequences of another person's wrongdoing. The physical contrast between swelling and suppuration gives a concrete image to unfair responsibility. No specific ancient reconstruction is asserted here.

word_family.gloss: 发出轻响；心中忽然闪过

senses.zh_definition: 发出像钟表运转时那样的滴答声或短促轻响。
senses.en_definition: To tick or make a short, light clicking sound.
senses.ms_definition: Berbunyi seperti bunyi jam dan sebagainya.
senses.nuances: 可描写连续的钟表声，也可描写单次短促轻响；不限定为计时器。[DBP PRPM](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=berdetik)

senses.zh_definition: 在心里暗自说；以内心独白的方式产生念头。
senses.en_definition: To say something inwardly or form an unspoken thought.
senses.ms_definition: Berkata di dalam hati.
senses.nuances: 常见于小说、叙事及内心独白，通常以 hati 为主语；不表示已经把话说出口。[DBP PRPM](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=berdetik)

senses.zh_definition: 因紧张、不安等情绪而心中悸动。
senses.en_definition: To flutter or throb with emotion, especially anxiety.
senses.ms_definition: Berdebar, berkenaan dengan hati atau perasaan.
senses.nuances: 偏文学表达，强调情绪上的悸动；日常交流中 berdebar 更直接自然，不宜把这里的 hati 理解为肝脏。[DBP PRPM](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=berdetik)

etymology.historical_story: The dictionary connects detik with a clock's small sound, a brief moment, and the stirrings of the heart. Berdetik carries that sound into action through ber-. These related meanings offer a useful cultural image: the quiet tick outside a person becomes an inward voice or emotional flutter. This explains the semantic connection, rather than establishing a dated historical origin.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 抓住 detik 里的 tik：钟表 tik-tik 地响，就是 berdetik；把轻响搬进心里，就能联想到内心独白和悸动。

word_family.gloss: 传统示哀用的白色头巾

senses.zh_definition: 佩戴示哀头巾或穿戴丧服，以表示哀悼。

senses.ms_definition: Memakai kain atau pakaian kabung sebagai tanda kesedihan atas sesuatu kematian.

senses.zh_definition: 服丧；哀悼，为某人的去世表现悲痛或遵行相应的纪念安排。

senses.nuances: 现代常见的广义用法，不要求佩戴某一种服饰。可用于家庭、机构或社会集体哀悼；不是一般“不开心”的同义词。参见 [DBP：berkabung](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=berkabung)。

etymology.historical_story: Kabung names a white cloth traditionally wound around the head as a sign of grief, including mourning a ruler. Adding ber- produces a verb associated with wearing that sign. The dictionary also records the broader meaning of displaying grief, allowing berkabung to describe mourning without specifying a particular garment. [DBP: perkabungan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=perkabungan), [DBP: berkabung](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=berkabung)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 kabung 记成一条示哀白布；ber- 表示处于相关状态或进行相关行为：ber- + kabung → 戴上示哀标志 → 服丧、哀悼。

morphology.pattern_note: ber- 表示具有某种资源或性质；接 tenaga 时保留 ber-，词根首音 /t/ 不脱落。ber- 和 tenaga 的首个 e 均读 /ə/。

senses.zh_definition: 有力量或精力的；精力充沛的；也指表达、表演或作品有力度、有感染力。
senses.en_definition: Having or displaying energy or strength; vigorous, powerful, or forceful in expression.
senses.ms_definition: Mempunyai atau memperlihatkan tenaga; ada tenaganya; berkekuatan; berdaya.
senses.nuances: 可描述身体状态，也可比喻演讲、文风和表演的力度。tidak bertenaga 表示没有力气，并不自动表示懒惰。描述 powered by 时通常还需说明能源，例如 bertenaga suria。

senses.zh_definition: 做事勤快、积极而有干劲的。
senses.en_definition: Active, industrious, and energetic in carrying out work or other activities.

senses.nuances: 此义着重持续投入和行动积极，与一般身体有力的意思相连。称赞工作表现时，最好结合具体贡献；bertenaga 不等于专业能力强或工作成果必然出色。

etymology.historical_story: Bertenaga is transparently built from tenaga, energy or strength, with ber-, expressing possession of that quality. Its dictionary meanings connect bodily strength with forceful creative expression and industrious activity. This semantic range offers a useful cultural image: the same word can describe someone ready for physical work and a performance that brings a stage to life. [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=bertenaga)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: tenaga 是“能量”，ber- 是“有”：bertenaga 就是“身上有能量”，人有精神，表演也有劲。

messages.zh: 可以，就是同一种。想切薄片也行。
messages.en: Yes, they're the same thing. You can slice them thinly if you like.

cultural_pragmatics.usage_etiquette: 地名正文须大写。食谱中的 bawang bombay 属另一使用环境，不要把城市名称和食材名称混译。

sociolinguistic_register.politeness_note: 谈当代城市、行程或行政事务时优先使用 Mumbai；引用历史文件、正式机构名称或作品名称时保留 Bombay。
sociolinguistic_register.usage_etiquette: 地名正文须大写。食谱中的 bawang bombay 属另一使用环境，不要把城市名称和食材名称混译。

etymology.historical_story: Bombay preserves a historical layer of the city's international naming. Portuguese records used Bombaim, and Bombay became established under British rule. The city adopted Mumbai in 1995, reconnecting its official name with a local naming tradition associated with Mumbadevi. Historical documents consequently retain Bombay even when modern geographical descriptions use Mumbai. [Mumbai City: History](https://mumbaicity.gov.in/en/history/)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 Bombay 和 Mumbai 成对记：同一座孟买，前者是旧名；bawang bombay 则联想厨房里的洋葱。

morphology.pattern_note: 直接基底为 bayaran，进一步词根为 bayar。-nya 是后附代词或回指成分，不是派生词缀；此处按模板归入 suffix。词干不变，ny 读 /ɲ/。音节为 ba.ya.ran.nya。所给 Jawi 实为 bayaran，未包含 -nya。

senses.zh_definition: 其应付或已付的款项、费用；具体付款人或所指事项由上下文确定。
senses.en_definition: The payment or fee associated with a previously mentioned person, service, or transaction.
senses.ms_definition: Wang yang dibayar atau perlu dibayar, dengan -nya merujuk kepada orang atau perkara yang telah disebut.
senses.nuances: bayaran 指款项，pembayaran 侧重付款过程。-nya 不表示付款已经完成，也不限定性别；须结合上下文理解为他的、她的或有关事项的。[DBP：bayaran](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=132444&keyword=bayaran)

senses.zh_definition: 某人因工作或提供服务而获得的薪酬、工钱或报酬。
senses.en_definition: His or her pay, wages, or remuneration for work or services.
senses.ms_definition: Gaji, upah atau wang yang diterima oleh seseorang sebagai balasan bagi kerja atau perkhidmatannya.
senses.nuances: 从收款人的角度表达所得报酬；不必是固定月薪，也可以是一次性服务费。

senses.zh_definition: 在名词后表示受雇、领酬的；附加 -nya 时，通常表示整个名词短语的所属关系。
senses.en_definition: Paid or hired, modifying a noun within a phrase whose possessor is indicated by -nya.
senses.ms_definition: Yang dibayar atau diupah untuk melakukan sesuatu; -nya menandakan hubungan milik bagi frasa nama berkenaan.
senses.nuances: 主要见于 tentera bayaran、serdadu bayaran 等结构；tentera bayarannya 指其雇佣兵，并非其军人的薪水。此义依赖前面的名词，不宜将 bayarannya 单独解释为雇员。

cultural_pragmatics.politeness_note: 询问服务费用可说 Boleh saya tahu jumlah bayarannya?，语气礼貌自然。询问私人薪资时应先判断关系与场合。
cultural_pragmatics.usage_etiquette: 适合收费、结算和报酬讨论。正式文件应交代收付款对象，避免 -nya 指代不清。不要用 orang bayaran 随意称呼普通雇员；该说法可能暗示受人收买。

sociolinguistic_register.politeness_note: 询问服务费用可说 Boleh saya tahu jumlah bayarannya?，语气礼貌自然。询问私人薪资时应先判断关系与场合。
sociolinguistic_register.usage_etiquette: 适合收费、结算和报酬讨论。正式文件应交代收付款对象，避免 -nya 指代不清。不要用 orang bayaran 随意称呼普通雇员；该说法可能暗示受人收买。

etymology.historical_story: Bayarannya illustrates how Malay builds useful expressions in layers: bayar names paying, bayaran names the money paid, and -nya connects that amount to someone or something already mentioned. The dictionary also preserves the paid-worker sense in serdadu bayaran. These related meanings connect everyday fees, earnings, and employment without requiring separate unrelated words. [DBP: bayaran](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=132444&keyword=bayaran)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 按 ba-ya-ran-nya 四拍记：bayar 付钱，bayaran 是款项，-nya 接上其所属——想到“他的报酬、那笔费用”。

senses.en_definition: A rhinoceros: a large, thick-skinned mammal of the family Rhinocerotidae, usually bearing one or two nasal horns.
senses.ms_definition: Sejenis mamalia dalam famili Rhinocerotidae yang berkulit tebal dan bersumbu.
senses.nuances: 单独使用通常指犀牛。部分传统复合名称不能按现代动物分类直译：badak air 是河马，badak tampung 可指马来貘，两者都不是犀科动物。[DBP：badak](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=82736&keyword=badak)。

senses.zh_definition: 用于 kuih badak 或 cucur badak，指以番薯和面粉制皮、包入调味椰丝等馅料后油炸的糕点。
senses.en_definition: In kuih badak or cucur badak, a fried sweet-potato dumpling with a savoury filling, typically seasoned grated coconut.
senses.ms_definition: Dalam nama kuih badak atau cucur badak, sejenis kuih goreng berkulit campuran ubi keledek dan tepung gandum serta berinti kelapa parut dan bahan perasa.
senses.nuances: 这是 DBP 另列的糕点用法，通常出现在完整食物名称中；名称不表示食材含犀牛肉。馅料配方可以不同。[DBP：badak II](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=82736&keyword=badak)。

etymology.historical_story: Badak is treated here as an independent Malay root; its deeper origin is not established by the supplied evidence. Its cultural reach is visible in traditional animal names: badak air denotes a hippopotamus, while badak tampung can denote a tapir. The dictionary separately records cucur badak as a snack, illustrating how familiar names travel beyond their basic zoological meaning.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 读 ba-da，最后用喉咙轻轻截住 [ʔ]；脑中定格一头厚皮犀牛。再记整词：badak air 是河马。

morphology.formula: ber- + henti → berhenti; berhenti + -kan → berhentikan; meN- + berhentikan → memberhentikan
morphology.pattern_note: 在已有词干 berhenti 后加使役后缀 -kan，词干不变；完整主动形式 memberhentikan 的 meN- 在 b 前实现为 mem-，b 保留。berhentikan 常见于祈使句或省略 meN- 的结构。输入 jawi 实为词根 henti 的拼写，此处按包保留，不能视为整个派生词的拼写。

senses.zh_definition: 使人、车辆或机器停止移动、运转或继续某项动作。
senses.en_definition: To cause a person, vehicle, or machine to stop moving, operating, or acting.
senses.ms_definition: Menyebabkan seseorang, kenderaan atau mesin tidak lagi bergerak atau beroperasi.
senses.nuances: berhenti 表示主体自己停下；berhentikan 带有使某对象停下的意思。普通主动陈述句一般用 memberhentikan；祈使句可用 Berhentikan kereta itu。释义依据完整形式整理，并非 DBP 对独立词头 berhentikan 的逐字定义。参见 [DBP：henti／memberhentikan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=berhenti)。

senses.zh_definition: 结束正在进行的活动、谈话或冲突。
senses.en_definition: To bring an ongoing activity, conversation, or conflict to an end.
senses.ms_definition: Mengakhiri kegiatan, percakapan atau pertelingkahan yang sedang berlangsung.
senses.nuances: 强调让某事不再继续；是否永久终止取决于语境。正式主动陈述句通常使用 memberhentikan；谈活动或过程时也常用 menghentikan。参见 [DBP：memberhentikan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=berhenti)。

senses.zh_definition: 终止某人的雇佣关系或职务；解雇或免职。
senses.en_definition: To terminate someone's employment or remove someone from a post.
senses.ms_definition: Menamatkan pekerjaan atau jawatan seseorang.
senses.nuances: 是他人或机构终止某人的任职，与本人 berhenti kerja（辞职）不同；不必然表示因违纪被开除。正式说明通常用 memberhentikan pekerja 或 pekerja diberhentikan。参见 [DBP：memberhentikan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=berhenti)。

cultural_pragmatics.politeness_note: 直接说 Berhentikan! 语气较强。请求司机或同事时可加 tolong、sila 或 ya，例如 Tolong berhentikan kereta di sini, ya。
cultural_pragmatics.usage_etiquette: 涉及终止雇佣时宜私下、清楚且尊重地说明原因，避免把 berhentikan 当作公开威吓用语；紧急制止危险时则适合简短明确的指令。

sociolinguistic_register.politeness_note: 直接说 Berhentikan! 语气较强。请求司机或同事时可加 tolong、sila 或 ya，例如 Tolong berhentikan kereta di sini, ya。
sociolinguistic_register.usage_etiquette: 涉及终止雇佣时宜私下、清楚且尊重地说明原因，避免把 berhentikan 当作公开威吓用语；紧急制止危险时则适合简短明确的指令。

etymology.historical_story: The modern word is best understood through the Malay henti family. Berhenti describes stopping, while memberhentikan makes another person or thing stop. In commands, the active prefix can be omitted, giving berhentikan. The same family also names stopping places through perhentian, linking everyday travel vocabulary with the broader idea of bringing movement or activity to an end.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 抓住 henti＝停：berhenti 是“停下来”，berhentikan 是“让它停下来”。把 -kan 想成伸手按下停止键。

morphology.pattern_note: 独立词根，无词缀，也不是重叠词。以下词族成员为以 bubur 为中心语的复合名称，不涉及词根音变。

senses.zh_definition: 粥；将米、玉米、豆类或其他淀粉类原料加水煮至软烂的食物，可为咸食或甜食。
senses.en_definition: A soft, moist dish made by cooking rice, grains, pulses, or similar ingredients in liquid; porridge, congee, or gruel.
senses.ms_definition: Sejenis makanan daripada beras, jagung, kacang hijau dan sebagainya yang lunak dan berair.
senses.nuances: 范围比中文日常所说的米粥更广，也包括绿豆甜粥等食品。bubur nasi 明确指米粥；bubur kacang hijau 通常是甜食。谚语 nasi sudah menjadi bubur 表示事情已经发生，无法恢复原状，并非另一个独立的食物义。释义依据：[DBP PRPM：bubur](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Search?k=bubur)。

sociolinguistic_register.usage_etiquette: 不要默认所有 bubur 都是咸米粥，点餐时宜说明种类。对刚遭遇损失的人直接说 nasi sudah menjadi bubur，可能显得冷淡或带有责备意味，应结合关系与语气使用。

etymology.historical_story: Bubur is established culinary vocabulary, not a modern Malay affix formation. Its cultural range extends from rice porridge to sweet mung bean preparations. The proverb nasi sudah menjadi bubur turns an everyday cooking transformation into an image of irreversible events: once rice has become porridge, the original grains cannot simply be restored. These uses are documented by [DBP PRPM](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Search?k=bubur).

etymology.historical_story: The dictionary’s physical definition of bingkai mentions wood and rattan, grounding the word in the practical task of strengthening an object around its edge. Modern terminology also uses bingkai for film and video frames. This offers a useful cultural bridge from tangible craft to moving images, although it does not establish the word’s ultimate historical origin. Both uses appear in [DBP PRPM](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=115704&keyword=bingkai).

etymology.historical_story: Sahabat belongs to the Arabic-derived vocabulary shared across Malay and Indonesian. The World Loanword Database connects it with Arabic ṣaḥāba[t-], referring to companions or friends, in the context of trade and Islamization. Malay then combines this established noun with ber- to express being friends, while persahabatan names the relationship itself. [WOLD](https://wold.clld.org/word/81311454766104371)

etymology.historical_story: English bunny developed as an affectionate diminutive of dialectal bun, a word associated with rabbits and earlier with squirrels. Its deeper origin remains uncertain. In Malay conversation, its occurrence is best understood as an English insertion rather than evidence of a Malay derivational family. [Etymonline](https://www.etymonline.com/word/bunny)

etymology.historical_story: Berkurangan belongs to the Malay family built around kurang, meaning less or insufficient. The family distinguishes a decrease occurring from someone actively causing a reduction: berkurangan describes the change, while mengurangkan expresses the action. This everyday distinction serves both household conversation and public reporting, from dwindling supplies to falling complaint numbers and easing discomfort.

etymology.historical_story: Bergelut is transparently formed from ber- and gelut. Its dictionary senses connect bodily wrestling with the effort of overcoming difficulties. That physical-to-abstract connection makes a useful cultural image: a person struggling to earn a living is pictured as grappling with resistance. The cited dictionary does not establish a deeper historical borrowing route. [PRPM: gelut](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=gelut)

etymology.historical_story: Beverly developed from an English surname associated with the Yorkshire place-name Beverley. etymology.historical_story: Buangan is transparently formed from buang, meaning to discard or expel, and the suffix -an. Its meanings connect objects thrown away with people expelled from a community or country. The expression kerajaan buangan extends that connection to a government operating abroad. This is a semantic explanation of the word's structure, rather than a claim about its earliest recorded use.

etymology.historical_story: English bass conceals two separate histories. The musical word developed from a word meaning low and now names low voices, parts, sounds, and instruments. The fish word goes back to Old English bears or bærs. Their shared spelling therefore hides different origins and pronunciations. Malay musical terminology uses bes, while English bass remains visible in music and equipment contexts. [American Heritage: bass](https://www.ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=BASS); [DBP: bes](https://prpmv1.dbp.gov.my/Search.aspx?d=1&k=bes)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 音乐 bass /beɪs/ 与英语 base 同音：想象低音托住整首歌的底座；鱼类 bass /bæs/ 则换成短元音，分开记。

etymology.historical_story: Berak is treated as an independent Malay root, despite its misleading resemblance to words beginning with the prefix ber-. Its cultural footprint extends beyond toilet talk: a traditional proverb asks who would admit defecating in the road, using embarrassment to illustrate people's reluctance to confess wrongdoing. [DBP dictionary](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=54140&keyword=berak)

etymology.historical_story: Bercium is transparently formed from ber- and cium. The dictionary preserves a revealing connection between smelling and affection: cium can involve drawing in breath near another person's cheek, as well as touching with the lips. This explains why older reunion descriptions combine embracing and bercium without necessarily describing romantic intimacy. [DBP reference](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=cium)

etymology.historical_story: Bakul names an object closely associated with weaving: the dictionary describes a container made from rattan, bamboo, and similar materials. Its cultural imagery also reaches into the saying masuk bakul angkat sendiri, which pictures someone climbing into a basket and lifting it themselves. The impossible action becomes a memorable image of self-praise. See [PKPS: the saying in use](https://www.pkps.gov.my/no-artikel-bil-13-2024-mari-kita-kekalkan-semangat-ketika-bekerja/).

etymology.historical_story: Oxford traces bullock to late Old English bulluc, a diminutive related to the word for bull. The earlier small-bull formation helps explain its association with young male cattle, while modern dictionary definitions emphasize castration. This is an English word history; it does not establish adoption into standard Malay. [Oxford word origin](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/us/definition/english/bullock)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 先用 bull 联想到公牛，再把 bullock 整词记作“年轻公牛，尤指阉牛”；读音约为“布勒克”，首音节重读。

morphology.pattern_note: -lah 是后附的强调或语气小品词，按本字段归入 suffix；附着时不引起词根音变。headword.jawi 按数据包保留，但 بيچارا 只对应 bicara，完整 bicaralah 应写作 بيچاراله。

etymology.historical_story: Bicara is traced to Sanskrit vicāra, associated with thought and discussion. Malay dictionaries preserve a related range covering opinions, deliberation, speech, and court proceedings. Bicaralah selects the speaking sense and adds the Malay particle -lah. Its tone can invite someone to open up or urge them to speak, depending on delivery. [Etymological reference](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/bicara).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 bi-ca-ra 分三拍念，再接 lah：像把话筒递给对方——“说吧！”记住 -lah 加语气，不表示过去或将来。

morphology.pattern_note: ber- 表示具有词根所指的品性或状态；词根不变。按输入的 be.ra.dab 划分，/r/ 与后面的元音组成音节；也可见按词素边界标示的 ber.a.dab。

word_family.gloss: 文明；社会文化的发展程度
具有文明的；文明发达的

senses.zh_definition: 有礼貌、有教养的；言谈举止合乎礼仪并尊重他人的。
senses.en_definition: Well-mannered and courteous in speech or behaviour.
senses.ms_definition: Mempunyai atau menunjukkan adab; berbudi bahasa dan bersopan.
senses.nuances: 强调待人接物的修养，不等同于学历高或社会地位高。这里按性质义标为 adjective；ber- 构式也可分析为表示状态的非及物谓语。tidak beradab 是较重的道德批评。[释义依据：DBP，adab／beradab](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=adab)。

senses.ms_definition: Telah maju tingkat kehidupan jasmani dan rohani; bertamadun.
senses.nuances: 多用于社会、民族或公共生活的论述。评判整个群体是否“文明”带有价值判断，宜明确所指的制度、行为或发展层面。[释义依据：DBP，adab／beradab](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=adab)。

etymology.historical_story: The base adab is borrowed from Arabic and concerns cultivated conduct and manners. Malay adds the productive prefix ber-, giving the meaning 'having or displaying adab'. The dictionary also records a broader sense concerning civilization. This creates a useful bridge between individual courtesy and collective cultural development, although the two senses depend on context. [Dictionary reference: DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=adab).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: ber-＝具有，adab＝礼仪；beradab 就是“身上有礼”，即有礼貌、有教养。

morphology.pattern_note: 词首 ber- 属于词根 berkat，不是此处另加的前缀；-i 接在词根后，末尾 t 成为下一音节的声母。输入的 headword.jawi 按要求保留，但 برکة 实际对应 berkat，不能视作已核实的 berkati 完整拼写。普通主动陈述用 memberkati；berkati 常用于祈祷、祈使或特定被动结构。

senses.zh_definition: 赐予某人或某事福佑、恩典或庇护；通过祈祷为其求福。
senses.en_definition: To bestow a blessing on someone or something, or invoke divine favour upon them.
senses.ms_definition: Memberikan berkat, rahmat atau restu kepada seseorang atau sesuatu.
senses.nuances: berkati 是动词，不等于名词 berkat，也不能解释为介词性的“幸亏”。祈祷中可直接说 Ya Tuhan, berkati…。普通陈述通常说 Tuhan memberkati…。释义依据 [DBP 的 berkat／memberkati 词条](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=254640&keyword=berkat+)，此处采用展开表述。

etymology.historical_story: Berkati combines the Malay suffix -i with berkat, a word of Arabic origin associated with barakah, or blessing. Its cultural life extends through prayers for families, journeys, livelihoods, and communal work. The derived verb focuses the blessing on a recipient, while keberkatan names the beneficial state or quality that people hope their actions will carry.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: berkat 是“福泽”，加 -i 就把福泽送向对象：berkati kami，赐福于我们。别把开头的 ber- 拆走。

morphology.pattern_note: -lah 是附着于前词的强调小品词，并非改变词类的派生后缀；接在 baca 后不引起辅音变化。headword.jawi 按输入保留词根写法 باچ，完整 bacalah 应包含 -lah，写作 باچله。

senses.zh_definition: 读吧；请阅读并理解文字内容。用于劝读、邀请或指示，也适用于阅读盲文。
senses.en_definition: Read; an imperative or exhortative form directing someone to understand written material.
senses.ms_definition: Bentuk suruhan atau ajakan supaya membaca dan memahami sesuatu yang tertulis atau tercetak, termasuk tulisan Braille.
senses.nuances: bacalah 通常用于指令或劝告，不等于陈述句中的 membaca。-lah 可表示鼓励、坚持或缓和语气，具体取决于语调。此处释义依据词根义及小品词功能综合编写，并非独立词条的逐字引文。[DBP：baca](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=baca)；[DBP：小品词连写规则](https://eseminar.dbp.gov.my/dokumen/ejaan.pdf)。

senses.zh_definition: 念出来吧；请朗读、诵读或吟诵文字、诗句、祷文等。
senses.en_definition: Read aloud or recite, as an instruction or encouragement.
senses.ms_definition: Bentuk suruhan atau ajakan supaya melafazkan tulisan, ayat, doa atau sajak secara lisan.
senses.nuances: 可指照着文字朗读，也可指念出熟记的祷文；诗歌和宗教语境对节奏、发音及礼仪有各自要求。此义依据 [DBP：baca](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=baca) 综合表述。

senses.zh_definition: 请读取仪表或测量装置显示的数值。
senses.en_definition: Read the value displayed by a meter or measuring instrument.
senses.ms_definition: Bentuk suruhan supaya melihat dan mengenal pasti angka atau nilai yang ditunjukkan oleh alat pengukur.
senses.nuances: 这里读取的是仪器示值，不一定需要出声；若要求记录，应另加 catat。依据 [DBP：baca 的仪表读数义](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=baca)。

senses.zh_definition: 请观察并揣摩人的表情、态度或内心意图。
senses.en_definition: Interpret someone's feelings, character or intentions from outward signs.
senses.ms_definition: Bentuk suruhan atau ajakan supaya memahami perasaan, sifat atau tujuan seseorang berdasarkan tanda yang dapat diperhatikan.
senses.nuances: 属于比喻用法，表示根据外在表现作判断，不表示能够确定知道他人的想法。依据 [DBP：baca 的推断义](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=baca)。

senses.zh_definition: 请看手相；通过观察掌纹占测命运。
senses.en_definition: Read someone's palm in the practice of palmistry.
senses.ms_definition: Bentuk suruhan supaya meneliti garis pada tapak tangan untuk meramalkan nasib menurut amalan tilikan.
senses.nuances: 是 baca 的专门搭配义，描述占卜实践；不表示掌纹具有经过证实的预测能力。依据 [DBP：baca tapak tangan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=baca)。

etymology.historical_story: The securely identifiable formation is baca followed by the attached particle -lah. Malay spelling guidance explicitly uses Bacalah to illustrate this joining rule. Its interest lies in the small particle: the reading action stays the same, while the speaker can encourage, insist or soften a direction. A deeper origin for baca is not established here.

etymology.historical_story: The tyre sense of ban reflects Dutch influence on Indonesian transport vocabulary: Dutch band became Indonesian ban. Malay dictionaries record this regional usage, while Malaysian speakers generally say tayar. A familiar vehicle part therefore preserves two different histories of European contact across neighbouring language communities, making the word especially useful when reading Indonesian manuals or discussing repairs across borders. [Royal Netherlands Academy](https://pure.knaw.nl/portal/files/474090/2006_Van_der_Sijs_Klein_Uitleenwoordenboek-def.pdf)

etymology.historical_story: Belerang belongs to a regional network of sulfur names that includes Javanese walirang. The Austronesian Comparative Dictionary discusses the spread of these forms through borrowing and suggests that Java's abundant sulfur supplied places where it was scarce. This history connects the word with inter-island exchange and older medicinal uses. [Austronesian Comparative Dictionary](https://ling.lll.hawaii.edu/dicts/ACD/acd-s_m.htm)

etymology.historical_story: English brand originally referred to burning wood or a torch. Its meanings expanded to marks made with heated iron, including marks identifying ownership or manufacture. From identifying marks, the word developed its commercial association with named goods. That history also explains the figurative verb: a damaging label can seem to leave a lasting mark on someone's reputation. See [Etymonline](https://www.etymonline.com/word/brand).

etymology.historical_story: Early European dictionaries recorded Malay using spellings that differ from modern conventions. Howison’s 1801 dictionary uses bree in expressions associated with giving, while a DBP-published study explicitly renders Bowrey’s bree as modern beri. This documents a historical spelling correspondence, rather than establishing bree as a separate modern headword. The packet alone cannot determine whether its token belongs to that historical usage. See [Howison’s dictionary](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/dc/A_dictionary_of_the_Malay_tongue%3B_James_Howison%2C_1801.pdf) and [the DBP study](https://dev.dbp.my/index.php/Melayu/ms/article/download/8345/4469/29950).

That label reveals an important feature of Malay dictionaries: they preserve vocabulary circulating across national borders, including words uncommon in Malaysian conversation. The packet establishes this regional association, but does not establish an earlier donor language or a dated borrowing history.

etymology.historical_story: Bersembang combines the Malay prefix ber- with sembang, a word associated with conversation. Its everyday setting is easy to picture: friends lingering over drinks, neighbours exchanging news, or colleagues talking after work. These settings illustrate its social meaning, rather than prove its historical origin. The supplied evidence establishes the formation but no earliest date or external source.

senses.zh_definition: 允许；使某事能够进行。须有句法语境支持，通常理解为 membolehkan 去掉主动前缀后的形式。
senses.en_definition: To allow or make possible; a prefixless form associated with membolehkan, requiring an appropriate grammatical context.
senses.ms_definition: Memberi izin atau menjadikan sesuatu dapat dilakukan; bentuk tanpa awalan yang berkaitan dengan membolehkan.
senses.nuances: 不能把独立出现的 bolehkan 一律当作规范陈述句中的主动谓语。正式主动句通常用 membolehkan 或 membenarkan。输入没有提供此拼写的独立 DBP 释义；本项是构词解释，不能据此认定其已获独立词目认证。[DBP：boleh 及其派生词](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?keyword=boleh)。

senses.zh_definition: 聊天连写形式，相当于 boleh, kan?，用来征求对方确认：可以，对吧？
senses.en_definition: An informal fused spelling of boleh, kan?, used to seek confirmation that something is acceptable or possible.
senses.ms_definition: Ejaan percakapan bagi ungkapan boleh, kan? yang digunakan untuk meminta pengesahan atau persetujuan.
senses.nuances: 此处 particle 指整个表达的确认功能；boleh 本身是情态助动词。标准书写应分开为 boleh, kan?。句首 bolehkan saya… 也可能误写了 bole hkah 中的疑问形式，正确拼写是 bolehkah saya…。仅凭孤立词形无法判定原意。

dual_scenarios.context: 公文 / 新闻 / 职场汇报
dual_scenarios.ms: Dalam laporan rasmi, ejaan “bolehkan” perlu diperiksa mengikut konteks: gunakan “bolehkah” untuk pertanyaan dan “membolehkan” untuk maksud memberikan izin atau menjadikan sesuatu dapat dilakukan.
dual_scenarios.zh: 正式报告中的“bolehkan”须按语境核查：提问用“bolehkah”，表示允许或使某事成为可能则用“membolehkan”。
dual_scenarios.en: In formal reports, check “bolehkan” against its context: use “bolehkah” for questions and “membolehkan” for allowing or enabling something.

etymology.historical_story: This spelling brings together two different Malay patterns rather than one securely established lexical history. The base boleh expresses possibility or permission; adding causative -kan underlies membolehkan. In informal messaging, however, the confirmation particle kan may also be attached directly to boleh. Context therefore determines whether the writer means allowing something or asking, “That is acceptable, right?”
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 先认 boleh＝可以，再看 kan 的任务：词尾 -kan 帮助表达“使可以”；句尾 kan? 则像中文“对吧？”。

etymology.historical_story: Malay builds berhantu transparently from hantu, meaning a ghost, and ber-, which can express having something or being in a particular state. This explains why the same formation describes both a haunted place and a person believed to be possessed. Ghost stories provide a memorable cultural setting, while the prefix supplies the grammatical meaning.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 先记 hantu＝鬼，再把 ber- 想成“有”：berhantu＝有鬼出没；描述人时可指被认为鬼附身。

morphology.pattern_note: ber- 表示具有某种属性，kualiti 保持原形；部分马来西亚口音弱化或不读 r，kua 可实现为较紧凑的 [kwa]。

etymology.historical_story: Kualiti is an English borrowing from quality, identified as English in DBP's thesaurus. Malay combines this borrowed noun with its own prefix ber- to form berkualiti. The result illustrates how an imported word enters ordinary Malay grammar and becomes useful for describing products, services, education, and the standard of everyday work.

etymology.historical_story: The name Baahubali belongs to a Sanskrit naming tradition associated with powerful arms. Bahubali is also a revered figure in Jain tradition. Modern cinema gave the name another prominent setting through Rajamouli's epic films. Shared naming does not establish a shared biography: the religious figure and the fictional characters require separate identification. [Jain educational source](https://jainworld.jainworld.com/JWEnglish/Jain%20story%20book.pdf), [film distributor](https://www.variancefilms.com/project/baahubali-the-epic)

sociolinguistic_register.politeness_note: 与来自缅甸的人交流时，可沿用对方自称的国家名称；不要仅凭 Burma 或 Myanmar 的选择推断其政治立场。
sociolinguistic_register.usage_etiquette: 历史讨论和原文引用可保留 Burma。现代马来语一般介绍国家时使用 Myanmar；引用机构、组织或作品名称时保留其正式名称。

etymology.historical_story: Burma and Myanmar refer to the same country, but their use reflects different historical and institutional naming choices. In June 1989, the authorities changed the country’s English name from Burma to Myanmar. Burma consequently remains important when reading older maps and records. Some institutions continued using it after the change, so it is not confined to pre-1989 texts. [Japan’s 1989 Diplomatic Bluebook](https://www.mofa.go.jp/policy/other/bluebook/1989/1989-3-2.htm), [UK country-name timeline](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/country-names/timeline-of-country-name-changes-in-hmg-use-1919-to-present)

etymology.historical_story: DBP records bengong as conversational Malay and explains it through bingung. That connection helps distinguish temporary confusion from the sharper insult heard in some conversations. The dictionary evidence establishes usage, rather than a dated borrowing history or an ancient root. Its deeper origin remains unverified here; a regional anecdote should not be presented as established etymology. [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=bingung)

senses.zh_definition: 谷物；供人食用、常作为基本粮食的禾本科作物籽粒，如小麦、大麦、玉米和稻谷。
senses.en_definition: Edible cereal grains, such as wheat, barley, maize, and rice, used as staple foods.
senses.ms_definition: Biji-bijian seperti gandum, barli, jagung dan padi yang dijadikan bahan makanan asas.
senses.nuances: 通常作集合名词，不必重叠表示复数。并非所有可食用种子都属于 bijirin；豆类通常另称 kekacang。在早餐语境中，也可借指谷物制成的早餐食品，但核心义不限于盒装早餐麦片。马来语释义据 [DBP PRPM：bijirin](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=bijirin) 展开缩写。

sociolinguistic_register.usage_etiquette: 点餐或购物时宜说明具体品类；bijirin 不保证食品无糖、无麸质或具有清真认证。

etymology.historical_story: Bijirin connects the vocabulary of farming with the language of everyday meals. DBP defines it through staple grains including rice, wheat, barley, and maize. Its modern uses therefore extend beyond packaged breakfast cereal. The consulted dictionary supplies its meaning, but does not establish a historical derivation that would justify treating -rin as a productive suffix. [DBP PRPM](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=bijirin)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 读 bi.ji.rin，想象一碗谷粒；用熟悉的 biji（籽粒）帮助联想，但不要把 -rin 当成可套用的后缀。

morphology.pattern_note: 整词作为现代马来语词根使用。加 meN- 或 peN- 时，b 保留，前缀分别实现为 mem- 和 pem-：membuli、pembuli。

senses.zh_definition: 欺凌、霸凌：通过威吓、羞辱、伤害或其他压迫行为欺负他人，尤其是较弱势者。
senses.en_definition: Bullying: intimidating, humiliating, or hurting another person, especially someone less powerful.
senses.ms_definition: Perbuatan mendera atau mempermainkan seseorang, terutama yang lemah, untuk menggertak, menakutkan atau mencederakannya.
senses.nuances: 现代常用概括义，涵盖肢体、言语、社交和网络欺凌。buli 指行为；指施害者须用 pembuli，不能直接套用英语名词 bully 的人物义。

senses.zh_definition: 以适应新环境或加入群体为名，对新成员实施的折磨、羞辱或恶整。

senses.ms_definition: Perbuatan mendera atau mempermainkan seseorang dengan alasan membiasakannya dengan suasana baharu.
senses.nuances: 对应输入包中与适应新环境有关的义项；所谓适应或迎新是施加行为的名义，并不表示这种做法合理或有益。

senses.zh_definition: 欺负、恐吓或伤害他人，尤其是较弱势者；相当于 membuli。
senses.en_definition: To bully, intimidate, or mistreat someone, especially someone less powerful.
senses.ms_definition: Mempermainkan atau mendera seseorang, biasanya yang lemah, untuk menggertak, mencederakan atau menakutkannya.
senses.nuances: 裸词动词常见于口语和禁令，如 Jangan buli。正式主动陈述通常使用 membuli，如 Mereka membuli pelajar itu。

etymology.historical_story: Buli is an adapted borrowing of English bully, with spelling suited to Malay. Once established, it entered Malay's productive affix system, giving membuli for the action and pembuli for the perpetrator. Dictionary descriptions include abusive initiation of newcomers, while contemporary Malaysian education discourse uses the word across physical, verbal, emotional, and online mistreatment.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 英语 bully 对应马来语 buli；记住三格：buli＝霸凌行为，membuli＝实施霸凌，pembuli＝霸凌者。

etymology.historical_story: Rather than being a separate ancient root, buatkannya combines the everyday verb buat with two productive grammatical elements. The ending -kan can introduce a beneficiary, while -nya supplies a third-person reference. A small household request therefore illustrates how Malay packages an action and its recipient into one written word. See [DBP: membuatkan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=membuatkan).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 按声音分块记：buat＝做，kan＝替人做，nya＝他或她；buat-kan-nya，就想到“替他做”。这是本义的记忆提示，其他语境也可表示“使他……”。

etymology.historical_story: Upaya belongs to Malay's Sanskrit-derived vocabulary, ultimately associated with upāya, meaning a means or resource. Crawfurd's 1852 dictionary already records upaya with meanings such as device, plan and resource. Malay ber- builds on that base, connecting the resources for achieving something with effort and capability. See [Crawfurd's dictionary](https://wallace-online.org/converted/pdf/1852_Crawfurd_WS5.2.pdf).

etymology.historical_story: Bahattar belongs to the Indo-Aryan numeral tradition. Historical linguistic research connects forms meaning seventy-two with Sanskrit dvāsaptati and related Prakrit forms. This history explains its South Asian connections, but does not establish borrowing into Malay. A Malay dictionary therefore needs separate evidence before treating this spelling as an accepted Malay word. [Historical study of Indo-Aryan numerals](https://fid4sa-repository.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/3154/1/Berger_Zahlwoerter_in_den_neuindoarischen_Sprachen_1986.pdf).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 bahattar、72、tujuh puluh dua 放在同一张记忆卡上：先认外语词形，再用马来语读出数字；不编造谐音或马来语词根。

morphology.formula: berdoa + -lah → berdoalah；内部结构：ber- + doa + -lah → berdoalah
morphology.pattern_note: 直接基底依输入为 berdoa，更深层词根是 doa（دعاء）。-lah 是附着语气词，本结构用 suffix 表示其后接位置，并非派生后缀；可加强或缓和劝请，取决于语境。输入音节缺失，补作 ber.do.a.lah。headword.jawi 按输入保留，但 بردعاء 对应 berdoa；完整 berdoalah 应加 له，写作 بردعاءله。

senses.zh_definition: 请祈祷吧；祈求上苍吧，用于劝勉、邀请或敦促对方祈祷。

senses.ms_definition: Meminta atau memohon kepada Tuhan, atau mengucapkan doa, dengan partikel -lah sebagai penegas atau pelembut suruhan.
senses.nuances: 基本词义来自 berdoa，-lah 增添劝请或强调语气，并未形成新的祈祷行为类别。berdoa 常接 kepada Tuhan、untuk 或 semoga；为某人祈祷可用 berdoa untuk seseorang。该词本身不专指伊斯兰教规定的礼拜 solat。[DBP 基词释义](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=202792&keyword=berdoa)。

etymology.historical_story: Doa comes from Arabic duʿāʾ, a supplication addressed to God. Malay integrates this religious noun through its own grammar: ber- forms the verb berdoa, and the attached particle -lah turns it into an exhortation. The resulting expression can sound warmly encouraging or solemnly insistent, depending on the relationship, setting, and speaker's tone. [Religious and linguistic background](https://www.muftiwp.gov.my/images/pdf/penerbitan/ebook/himpunandoasiri2/Himpunan_30_Doa_Menghadapi_Dugaan_Dan_Musibah.pdf).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: doa＝祷告；berdoa＝进行祷告；末尾加 lah，像中文加一句“吧”：berdoalah＝祈祷吧。

etymology.historical_story: Berkilau is transparently formed from kilau, the Malay noun for a gleam or glittering light, with the prefix ber-. Its imagery connects stars, gemstones, polished metal, and sunlit water. The related noun kilauan names the gleam itself, while berkilau presents the object as shining. This contrast makes the word family easy to visualize.

etymology.historical_story: Malay balet belongs to the international vocabulary of ballet. French ballet ultimately reflects Italian balletto, a diminutive associated with dance. The art developed through European court entertainment before becoming a professional stage tradition. The consulted evidence does not establish the immediate donor language or date of entry into Malay. See [Philharmonie de Paris](https://pad.philharmoniedeparis.fr/la-musique-de-ballet-de-la-renaissance-au-xviiie-siecle.aspx?_lg=fr-FR).

morphology.pattern_note: buleh 是 boleh 的方言形式，见于 DBP 北部方言例句；首音节元音写作 u，不涉及加缀。以下词族按标准形式 boleh 构成。

senses.zh_definition: 能；能够。标准马来语 boleh 的方言形式，表示具备做某事的能力或条件。
senses.en_definition: Can; be able to: a dialectal form of Malay boleh expressing ability or practical possibility.
senses.ms_definition: Bentuk dialek bagi boleh yang bermaksud dapat atau mampu melakukan sesuatu.
senses.nuances: 马来语语法中属于 kata bantu ragam，即情态助动词；此处依给定词性集合归入 verb。DBP 的吉打及槟城方言材料可见 buleh，但这不等于它是正式书面语的标准拼写。正式写作使用 boleh 或按语义选用 dapat。[DBP PRPM：北部方言例句](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=226380&keyword=leh)

senses.zh_definition: 可以；获准。标准马来语 boleh 的方言形式，表示某个行为得到允许。
senses.en_definition: May; be allowed to: a dialectal form of boleh expressing permission.
senses.ms_definition: Bentuk dialek bagi boleh yang bermaksud dibenarkan atau diizinkan melakukan sesuatu.
senses.nuances: 疑问句可用于请求许可，单独回答 Buleh 也可表示同意。此释义依据标准词 boleh 编写，并非 buleh 的独立官方释义；正式对应形式为 Boleh。[DBP PRPM：boleh](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=128916&keyword=boleh+)

etymology.historical_story: Buleh illustrates the difference between a regional spoken form and a standard written form. DBP’s northern dialect materials contain sentences using buleh alongside standard Malay equivalents with boleh. These records support its regional use, but they do not establish a separate ancient root or a precise date of origin. Its dictionary treatment should therefore preserve the connection with boleh. [DBP dialect examples](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=226380&keyword=leh)

headword.verification_note: 原始小写词形的具体所指尚未确认。以下提供有马来西亚官方用例支持的 BEV 汽车缩写义，不能据此断定原始语料中的 bev 必然具有此义。

morphology.formula: 若指汽车术语：Battery Electric Vehicle → BEV
morphology.pattern_note: BEV 是英语词组的首字母缩写，不是由马来语词根加词缀构成。原始 bev 的身份未定，故保留数据包的根词字段，不据此认定它是马来语本族词根。

senses.zh_definition: 仅在原词确指大写缩写 BEV 时：纯电动汽车，即依靠可充电电池供电、不配备内燃发动机的车辆。
senses.en_definition: If intended as BEV: a battery electric vehicle powered entirely by rechargeable batteries, without an internal combustion engine.

senses.nuances: 此义在马来西亚汽车和政策语境中有据，标准写法为 BEV。以下搭配及例句均以这一解释为前提；不能将它泛化为所有小写 bev 的含义。马来语释义为编辑性概括。[MITI：BEV 指南](https://www.miti.gov.my/miti/resources/Approve%20Permit/Motor%20vehicle/Garis_Panduan_AP_Peneraju_Global_BEV.pdf)；技术定义见 [Liberty 马来语文件](https://www.libertyinsurance.com.my/images/pdf/lib/ev-365-care-endorsement-bm.pdf)。

etymology.historical_story: In Malaysian automotive documents, BEV abbreviates the English phrase Battery Electric Vehicle. Its appearance in Malay illustrates the use of international technical initials alongside a Malay explanatory term, kenderaan elektrik bateri. This documented usage establishes an automotive interpretation, but cannot identify an isolated lowercase bev without its original context. etymology.historical_story: Bip closely echoes the short electronic sound it names and corresponds to English beep. Malay dictionary usage places it in bunyi bip, making the audible signal central to its meaning. Scanners, phones and household appliances provide familiar modern settings for the word. These connections explain its memorability without establishing a particular borrowing date or transmission route. [English–Malay dictionary](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english-malaysian/beep)

senses.zh_definition: 闪耀；发出闪电或像闪电一样短暂、强烈的光。

senses.zh_definition: 发亮；呈现光滑、明亮或闪闪反光的状态，常形容擦亮的鞋、金属及光泽明显的表面。
senses.en_definition: To shine or have a glossy, gleaming, or polished appearance.
senses.ms_definition: Bersinar-sinar, bercahaya, berkilap atau berkilauan.
senses.nuances: 这是日常最常见的用法。通常描述光泽或反光，并不表示物体自身发光。可以形容擦亮的皮鞋，也可以形容光亮的布料；发亮本身不保证干净或安全。

etymology.historical_story: Kilat names lightning, a striking image of sudden brightness. With ber-, the word can describe flashing light, but its dictionary meanings also include the gleam of polished surfaces. Shiny shoes, metal blades, and lustrous clothing bring that imagery into everyday life. The connection provides a memorable semantic bridge between a bright flash and a surface that catches the light.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: kilat＝闪电；berkilat＝带着闪电般的亮光。想象皮鞋擦到像闪电一样闪亮。

etymology.historical_story: Two unrelated histories meet in the spelling bit. In food vocabulary, it names the beet plant, including red beetroot and sugar beet; the supplied evidence does not establish its precise borrowing route. In computing, DBP explicitly identifies bit as a shortening of English binary digit. Remembering the vegetable beside the two symbols 0 and 1 keeps these separate origins distinct. [DBP: bit II](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=digit)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 读作近似“必特”：菜篮里是一颗甜菜，电脑里是一位 0 或 1；用场景区分两个 bit。

etymology.historical_story: Bernas belongs to the vocabulary of fullness and agricultural productivity. Its concrete senses concern well-filled grain and productive rice plants; its figurative sense describes speech or thought with substance. A useful cultural reading connects these meanings: just as a grain should contain something valuable inside, a worthwhile contribution should offer more than an impressive exterior. This is a semantic illustration, not a dated origin claim.

etymology.historical_story: Billion developed in French through an alteration of million involving bi-, meaning twice. Its numerical value has differed between counting systems, which explains why older sources can disagree by a factor of one thousand. Contemporary English commonly uses the short-scale value of one thousand million; Malay uses the adapted spelling bilion. [Académie française](https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A9B1128)；[OECD](https://www.oecdnea.org/upload/docs/application/pdf/2020-01/dir1/oecd_style_guide_english.pdf)；[PRPM](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=274052&keyword=billion)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 现代英语 billion：1 后面九个零＝十亿；写马来语 bilion，l 只留一个。

etymology.historical_story: English bush, in its plant sense, belongs to a Germanic word family associated with shrubs and woodland. Neither history establishes standard Malay usage, and a surname occurrence would require its own identification from the original context. morphology.pattern_note: -lah 是附着于前词并连写的强调小品词，不是派生后缀；本字段因此记 none。词根无音位替换，增加音节 /lah/；ng 表示单一辅音 /ŋ/。[DBP 语法说明](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?d=175768&keyword=perlu+lah)。

senses.zh_definition: 醒来；从睡眠中起来。加 -lah 可表示催促、劝请或叙事强调。
senses.en_definition: To wake or get up from sleep, with exhortative or emphatic -lah.
senses.ms_definition: Terjaga atau bangun daripada tidur, dengan penegasan oleh partikel -lah.
senses.nuances: 日常叫醒他人更常说 bangunlah。bangkitlah 可带较郑重或文学性的语气；-lah 的具体力度取决于语调。

senses.zh_definition: 从坐姿或卧姿起身；站起来。
senses.en_definition: To rise from a sitting or lying position.

senses.zh_definition: 复活；从死亡状态恢复生命。

senses.ms_definition: Hidup semula selepas mati.
senses.nuances: 用于宗教叙述、文学或超自然故事。bangkitlah dalam叙事中可表示强调，不必解释为向死者发出的命令。

senses.zh_definition: 升起；扬起，尤指尘土等向空中上升。
senses.en_definition: To rise into the air, especially of dust.
senses.ms_definition: Naik ke udara, misalnya debu.
senses.nuances: 带 -lah 时多见于文学性叙事，例如 maka bangkitlah debu；普通新闻陈述通常直接使用 bangkit 或 berterbangan。

senses.zh_definition: 产生；涌现，指情绪、勇气或其他内在状态出现。
senses.en_definition: To arise or stir, of a feeling or inner state.
senses.ms_definition: Timbul atau terbit sesuatu perasaan atau keadaan dalam diri.
senses.nuances: 常以情绪名词作主语。bangkitlah kemarahannya 属叙事强调；表示使别人产生某种情绪时，通常改用 membangkitkan。

senses.zh_definition: 膨起；发起，指面糊或面团体积增大。
senses.en_definition: To rise or expand, of dough or batter.
senses.ms_definition: Mengembang atau bertambah isi padu, berkenaan adunan.
senses.nuances: 这是词根 bangkit 的烹饪义。带 -lah 的完整形式在此义中较少见，多需叙事强调语境；日常食谱更常使用 naik 或 mengembang。以下为说明性组合，不代表高频固定搭配。

senses.zh_definition: 觉醒并奋起；从挫折、衰弱或落后状态中振作，重新争取进步。

senses.ms_definition: Sedarkan diri dan bertindak untuk maju, atau kembali berusaha selepas mengalami kemerosotan atau kegagalan.
senses.nuances: 常见于激励、演说、体育和社会议题。bangkitlah semula 是振作的号召；是否含反抗意味须由上下文决定。

etymology.historical_story: The expressive force of bangkitlah comes from combining a verb of rising with the attached particle -lah. Physical rising also supplies an image for renewed courage and collective recovery. This explains its usefulness in motivational speech without requiring a separate ancient origin for the complete form. [DBP: bangkit](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=123312&keyword=bangkit).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 bangkit 想成身体“站起来”，再把 lah 听成一句鼓励的“吧”：bangkitlah＝起来吧、振作吧。

etymology.historical_story: English buck has several histories, so a single origin story would mislead. The animal noun continues Old English forms for male goats and deer. The dollar sense may be connected with buckskin used in exchange, but that explanation remains qualified. A person named Buck requires separate identification and may have a different naming history. [Dictionary.com](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/buck)

senses.zh_definition: 贝尔；表示功率比等量的对数级单位，符号为 B；一贝尔等于十分贝。
senses.en_definition: The bel, symbol B, a logarithmic unit for expressing levels such as power ratios, equal to ten decibels.
senses.ms_definition: Unit logaritma berlambang B untuk menyatakan aras berasaskan nisbah, misalnya nisbah kuasa; satu bel bersamaan sepuluh desibel.
senses.nuances: 马来语工程术语表收录 bel。此处马来语释义为技术综合释义，并非逐字引用 DBP 定义。贝尔表示对数级，不是频率单位；功率比为 10∶1 时，级差为 1 B。实际应用更常使用 desibel。参见 [工程术语表：bel](https://sps.utem.edu.my/phocadownloadpap/Istilah%20Kejuruteraan.pdf)及 [SLB 技术词汇：bel](https://glossary.slb.com/terms/b/bel)。

senses.zh_definition: 木橘树，学名 Aegle marmelos；马来语也称 maja 或 bila。
senses.en_definition: The bael tree, Aegle marmelos, also called maja or bila in Malay.
senses.ms_definition: Sejenis pokok bernama saintifik Aegle marmelos, yang juga dikenali sebagai maja atau bila.
senses.nuances: DBP 在 maja 及 maja batu 条目中将 bel 列为植物别名；此义与计量单位义应分别处理。所列植物搭配用于说明树与果实，未宣称其具有高语料频率。参见 [DBP PRPM：bel 的相关植物记录](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=bel)。

etymology.historical_story: The technical unit bel commemorates Alexander Graham Bell and belongs to the vocabulary of acoustic and electrical signal measurement. Its smaller form, the decibel, is more familiar in practice. Malay also records bel as a name for Aegle marmelos; that botanical meaning must be kept separate, because the shared spelling does not establish a shared origin. [SLB: bel](https://glossary.slb.com/terms/b/bel), [DBP records](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=bel)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 技术义记 Bell → bel → 贝尔，再记 desi-＝十分之一，所以 1 bel＝10 desibel；植物义另配木橘树图像记忆。

etymology.historical_story: Bane goes back to Old English bana, associated with a killer or something bringing death. Older meanings included poison and destruction, and the poisonous sense survives in plant names such as wolfsbane. Modern speakers often soften that dark inheritance into humorous complaint: an everyday nuisance becomes the bane of their life. [Sources: Oxford](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/bane), [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/bane).

etymology.historical_story: Malay turns the noun hasrat, a strong wish, into a verb by adding ber-, presenting the speaker as someone who holds that wish. DBP illustrates the word with an ambition to reach university. This educational setting offers a useful cultural association: berhasrat gives a personal dream the measured tone of a publicly expressed intention. [DBP: hasrat](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=10456&keyword=hasrat)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 hasrat 记成心里的愿望，再加表示“具有”的 ber-：berhasrat，就是“心里怀着愿望”。
